discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception, construction and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 prize honoured the theoretical prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism, but the 2012 discovery that confirmed it was an experimental achievement of the first rank. Peter Jenni and Tejinder Virdee were founding architects of ATLAS and CMS, shaping detector concepts able to isolate the decisive diphoton and four-lepton signals from overwhelming backgrounds. Fabiola Gianotti led ATLAS through the discovery, ensuring the rigour and systematic control that made the 5-sigma claim unassailable. Since then, both experiments have measured Higgs couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and now muons, establishing it as the elementary scalar of the Standard Model and opening the path to the Higgs self-coupling and the shape of the Higgs potential, our window on the electroweak phase transition. This discovery tells us something definite about the fundamental structure of nature; its experimental pioneers deserve recognition.
